# A path parameter with a type other than string.
#
# The parameters are a declared struct, so a field says what it is and the
# route parses the segment into it. Nothing could say this before: the
# placeholders in the href *were* the declaration, and the checker synthesized
# a string var per name, so a page number arrived as text and every use of it
# converted.
#
# A segment that does not parse leaves the field at the struct's zero rather
# than failing the request. That is the same answer a missing field gets, and
# the route has no other: the mux has already matched, so there is a page to
# render and the only question is what it renders with.
#
# It has to compile, which is the whole point of the type: `v.Page + 1` is Go
# integer arithmetic, and a grep over the generated source would not have said
# whether the binding produced an int at all.

sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out app.sngl

exec go build ./...

grep 'v.Slug = __r.PathValue\("slug"\)' out/server.go
grep 'strconv.Atoi\(__r.PathValue\("page"\)\)' out/server.go
grep 'Page int' out/server.go

# The redirect names the page the browser should ask for next, so a numeric
# parameter is spelled back the way the path spelled it.
grep 'url.PathEscape\(strconv.Itoa\(v.Page\)\)' out/server.go

-- go.mod --
module typedparam

go 1.24

-- srv/srv.go --
package srv

func Bump(n int) int { return n + 1 }

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "go:typedparam/srv"
import "sngl:platform/html"

struct PageParams {
    slug string
    page int
}

var hits = 0

window #page(title="t", href=`/p/{slug}/{page}`, params=PageParams{}) {
    component content(v) {
        html.button(innerText="go", @click { hits = srv.Bump(hits) })
        html.span(innerText="{v.slug} {v.page + 1} {hits}")
    }
}
